eaa.heading: The European Accessibility Act is here.
eaa.body: Since 28 June 2025, websites operating in the EU must meet the Act's accessibility requirements.
eaa.notSure: Not sure whether your site meets them? We can help.
eaa.doorLine: If everyone can't use the door, is it truly an entrance?
details.heading: The EAA deadline has passed.
details.body: The European Accessibility Act has applied to EU websites since 28 June 2025. Enforcement and penalties are set by each country's own law.
affected.heading: Who's affected
affected.exempt: Companies with fewer than 10 employees and annual revenue under {threshold} are exempt.
affected.exceptionIntro: The exemption does not cover companies offering products that carry accessibility requirements of their own, such as:
affected.exceptionDevices: consumer electronics — smartphones, ATMs, e-book readers, and the like
a11y.heading: Accessibility
a11y.lede: Accessibility is a human right. No exceptions.
a11y.online: Life has moved online. We depend on the internet for work, connection, and daily necessities. It is entertainment, but it is also essential.
a11y.houseLine: When you build a house, you don't make the door optional. Digital access works the same way.
a11y.captions: You have probably used an accessible feature without noticing. Captions in a noisy room. Dictation while driving. Voice commands with your hands full.
a11y.curbCuts: Curb cuts help wheelchair users. They also help parents with strollers, travellers with luggage, and delivery workers with hand trucks.
a11y.closing: Good accessible design does not help only some people. It makes the experience better for everyone.
legal.body: Since 28 June 2025, accessibility is law across Europe. Germany has the BFSG, the EU has the European Accessibility Act, and the UK works through the Equality Act 2010.
legal.standard: All of them point at the same technical standard: WCAG 2.1 Level AA.
legal.enforcement: Enforcement differs by country. Consumers and advocacy groups can ask authorities to inspect a site, and can take legal action if barriers stay unfixed.
who.heading: Who needs accessibility?
who.intro: Accessibility is not only for people with permanent disabilities. At some point, all of us need these features.
who.motorDesc: A broken arm, carrying groceries, holding a baby
who.visualDesc: Forgotten glasses, a cracked screen, sun glare on a laptop
who.auditoryDesc: A loud café, an ear infection, a dead headphone battery
who.cognitiveDesc: Tired after a long day, stressed and distracted, trying to multitask
who.closing: Sound familiar? That is because accessible design helps all of us.
what.heading: What makes a website accessible?
what.intro: Accessible websites follow four principles from the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG):
what.perceivableDesc: Everyone can reach your information, even without the use of every sense
what.operableDesc: Every function works for everyone, with no exceptions
what.understandableDesc: The content is clear and the navigation makes sense
what.robustDesc: The site works on any device, with any assistive technology, now and later
apply.heading: Does this apply to my business?
apply.intro: If you operate in the EU and your website does any of the following, the Act applies to you:
apply.books: Allows people to book appointments or reservations
apply.services: Provides banking, transport, or media services
apply.updated: Was updated or published after 28 June 2025
apply.includes: That covers e-commerce sites, booking platforms, SaaS companies, restaurants taking orders online, and more.
apply.exemption: The one exemption: companies with fewer than 10 employees and annual revenue under {threshold}.
apply.smallBiz: Small businesses are not always exempt. Sell smartphones, tablets, or e-readers and the requirements apply whatever your size.
apply.notSureLead: Not sure whether this applies to you?
apply.notSureTail: and we will help you work it out.
services.heading: Services
services.body: We work in accessible web design, brand development, and content strategy. Your website should outlast this year's stack and work for everyone.
services.doorMetaphor: Think of it this way. A door that only opens for someone {height} tall is not a broken door. It is a badly designed one.
approach.focusedDesc: Messages are clear, obvious, and worth the reader's time
approach.userCenteredDesc: Navigation is smooth, predictable, and inclusive
approach.futureProofDesc: Content is purposeful, adaptable, and cost-effective
closing.wcag: Our principles follow the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), the international standard for accessible websites.
